public_rationale: Ramp data, as PYMNTS reported, says the top 1% of business customers account for 80% of enterprise spending at both OpenAI and Anthropic. That matches his 80% figure. But Ramp measures spending by its own business customers. It is not the labs' revenue, and neither lab has disclosed customer-level concentration. 'Vast majority of total revenues' fits Anthropic, where an analyst estimate puts the API share at about 80%. For OpenAI, a mid-2026 report has enterprise revenue only just passing consumer revenue, which is a slim majority. The speaker hedged the customer count and the VC-backed share, so those parts are not scored. The firm parts are partly backed by an outside estimate and partly in doubt for OpenAI. Whether this counts as a failure depends on whether 'vast majority' applies to each lab or to both combined, which he did not say. The evidence does not settle the claim.
limitations: All the figures are press-reported estimates. None is audited.
OpenAI's enterprise share comes from one anonymous account of an investor meeting.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic's enterprise revenues, which make up the vast majority of their total revenues, depend on what are likely hundreds of customers spending outsized amounts on AI tokens, an indeterminately-large chunk of them AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them.
conditions: what are likely hundreds of customers

statement.excerpt: This means that 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic’s enterprise revenues — which make up the vast majority of their total revenues — are dependent on what are likely hundreds of customers spending outsized amounts of money on AI tokens, with an indeterminately-large chunk of them being AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them.

which make up the vast majority of their total revenues
dependent on what are likely hundreds of customers spending outsized amounts of money on AI tokens
an indeterminately-large chunk of them being AI startups that can only do so as long as venture capital supports them
our_interpretation: The firm parts are two: (a) about 80% of each lab's enterprise revenue comes from a small set of top customers, and (b) enterprise revenue is the vast majority of each lab's total revenue.
The 'likely hundreds' customer count and the 'indeterminately-large chunk' of VC-backed startups are hedged by the speaker. They are not scored as thresholds.
The post builds on Ramp's data on business spending, so the 80% figure is read as a statement about the labs' real enterprise revenue, which the Ramp sample estimates.
He describes an ongoing state with no named period. The target period is the most recent window public evidence could cover before the post: July 2026 to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable evidence that about 80% of each lab's actual enterprise revenue comes from a few hundred top customers, and that enterprise revenue is the vast majority of total revenue at both labs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence that enterprise revenue is spread much more widely than this at either lab, or that enterprise revenue is not the vast majority of total revenue (for example, roughly half or less at OpenAI).
